# Land Cover Classification

The goal of this project is to play with land cover classification algorithms and gain more experience in building them.

## Packages

```{r Packages}
#| echo: True
#| eval: True
#| message: False
#| warning: False

library(tidyverse)
library(rstac)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(mapedit)
library(leaflet)
```

## Step 1: Get Some Data

First order of business is to get myself some data to work with. To do this, I am going to use `rstac` to pull data from Microsoft Planetary Computer for the Gallatin Valley.

This cell sets up the source and lists the available data sets from that source.

```{r STAC_Source}
#| echo: True
#| eval: False

# Set the source to Planetary Computer
stac_source <- stac('https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/')

# Set up a collections query
collections_query <- collections(stac_source)

# Execute the collections query
PC_collections <- get_request(collections_query)

# List the collections in human readable format
PC_collections["collections"]

# Data can also be browsed at this link https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/catalog
```

Now I need to decide on a data set. I think to start I am going to look at sentinel-2 data.

```{r STAC_Search}
#| echo: True
#| eval: False

# Define an area of interest over the Gallatin Valley
aoi <- c(-110.8665, 45.6074, -111.2307, 45.8274)

# Search for relevant imagery
results <- stac_search(
  q = stac_source,
  collections = "sentinel-2-l2a",
  bbox = aoi,
  datetime = "2025-07-01/2025-07-10",
  limit = 999
  ) %>% 
  get_request()
```

Now to download some imagery and see what we're working with.

```{r STAC_Download}
#| echo: True
#| eval: False

# Define the query I want to download after browsing the results list
executed_stac_query <- stac_search(
  q = stac_source,
  collections = "sentinel-2-l2a",
  ids = c("S2C_MSIL2A_20250708T181941_R127_T12TWR_20250708T232313",
          "S2A_MSIL2A_20250707T181801_R084_T12TWR_20250708T010421")
  ) %>% 
  get_request()

# Sign the query for rate-limiting purposes
signed_stac_query <- items_sign(
  executed_stac_query,
  sign_planetary_computer()
)

# List of all the assets available for sentinel-2-l2a
assets_list <- c("AOT", "B01", "B02", "B03", "B04", "B05", "B06", "B07", "B08", "B09", "B11", "B12", "B8A", "SCL", "WVP", "visual", "safe-manifest", "granule-metadata", "inspire-metadata", "product-metadata", "datastrip-metadata", "tilejson", "rendered_preview")

# Download the assets
assets_download(
  items = signed_stac_query,
  asset_names = assets_list,
  output_dir = "~/remote_sensing/land_class/data",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

```

Beautiful, we now have some data. Let's plot it and see what it looks like.

```{r Plot_The_Data}
#| echo: True
#| eval: True

# List file paths for first image set
file_list1 <- list.files("./data/sentinel2-l2/12/T/WR/2025/07/07/S2A_MSIL2A_20250707T181801_N0511_R084_T12TWR_20250708T010421.SAFE/GRANULE/L2A_T12TWR_A052448_20250707T181804/IMG_DATA/R10m/", full.names = T)

# List file paths for secpnd image set
file_list2 <- list.files("./data/sentinel2-l2/12/T/WR/2025/07/08/S2C_MSIL2A_20250708T181941_N0511_R127_T12TWR_20250708T232313.SAFE/GRANULE/L2A_T12TWR_A004387_20250708T182843/IMG_DATA/R10m/", full.names = T)

# Set first raster image
rgb1 <- rast(file_list1[2:4])

# Set second raster image and reproject to WGS84
rgb2 <- rast(file_list2[2:4]) %>% 
  project("epsg:4326")

# Set true color image for second raster
tci <- rast(file_list2[6])

# Plot 
#plotRGB(rgb2, stretch = "lin")

#plot(tci)
```

Okay, I like the look of rgb2 well enough to move forward with it to some unsupervised classification. I am going to attempt to run k-means classification on the entirety of this raster, although i may add in band 8 to give it more data to work with.

```{r K_Means_5}
#| echo: True
#| eval: False

# Set the seed to make the results reproducible
set.seed(69)

# Define the cluster raster with NIR
cluster_buster <- rast(file_list2[2:5])

# Run the k_means() functiion on it
kmcluster <- k_means(cluster_buster, centers = 5)

# View
plot(kmcluster)

# Save the raster
writeRaster(kmcluster, "./products/k_means_5_centers_4_bands_10m.tif")
```

Not too shabby, but also not the world's most enlightening map. I have to wonder if it might not be more effective to reduce the number of potential classes. Let's run it again with only 3 clusters and see what that looks like.

```{r K_Means_3}
#| echo: True
#| eval: False

# Run the k_means() functiion
kmcluster3 <- k_means(cluster_buster, centers = 3)

# View
plot(kmcluster3)

# Save the raster
writeRaster(kmcluster3, "./products/k_means_3_centers_4_bands_10m.tif")
```

Well, that's atrocious. 🤮 Clearly, 3 clusters is not enough. I doubt 7 clusters would make it better, either. Let's just move on to supervised classification.

First step is to make some polygons I can sample for cal/val data. I tried resampling to a lower resolution so I could draw my land cover polygons directly on the satellite imagery I am using, but leaflet really doesn't like the size of my area of interest and I had to resample too much for it to be useful. There are ways around that, of course, but I am not sure they are worth the effort at the moment. The main goal was to be able to determine which fields specifically are irrigated vs unirrigated in my imagery.

```{r Supe_Class}
#| echo: True
#| eval: False

# Reproject the raster into WGS84 and get the extent
raster_extent <- ext(rgb2)

# Convert the extent into a vector
extent_vect <- vect(raster_extent) %>% 
  set.crs("epsg:4326")

# Sanity check
plot(extent_vect)

# True color image for reference
plot(tci)

# Define a leaflet map with the bbox of the raster
draw_map <- leaflet() %>% 
  addProviderTiles(provider = "Esri.WorldImagery") %>%
  addPolygons(data = extent_vect, fill = F)

# Draw some plots for cal/val data  
irrigated_polygons <- drawFeatures(draw_map)
rangeland_polygons <- drawFeatures(draw_map)
alpine_polygons <- drawFeatures(draw_map)
forest_polygons <- drawFeatures(draw_map)
water_polygons <- drawFeatures(draw_map)
built_polygons <- drawFeatures(draw_map)

# Put 'em in a list
samps <- list(irrigated_polygons, rangeland_polygons, alpine_polygons, 
     forest_polygons, water_polygons, built_polygons)

# Make a matching list of land cover types
samp_types <-list("irrigated", "rangeland", "alpine", 
                  "forest", "water", "built")

# Define a func to convert to SpatVector with a type column
samp_vect_func <- function(polygon, lcover_type) {
  polygon %>% 
    mutate(type = lcover_type) %>% 
    vect()
}

# Run the func
samp_vect_list <- map2(samps, samp_types, samp_vect_func)

# Create some lists for use in map()
sample_polygons <- c(irrigated_polygons, rangeland_polygons, alpine_polygons, forest_polygons, water_polygons, built_polygons)
sample_names <- c("irrigated_polygons", "rangeland_polygons", "alpine_polygons", "forest_polygons", "water_polygons", "built_polygons")


# Write my sample polygons to disk
map2(sample_polygons,
     sample_names,
     \(x, y) writeVector(x, 
                         filename = paste0("./data/sample_polys/", y), 
                         filetype = "KML", 
                         overwrite = T)
)

# Check to make sure it worked
billy_bob <- vect("./data/sample_polys/rangeland_polygons")

draw_map %>% 
  addPolygons(data = billy_bob)
```

Well, that last step was very messy and I'm sure if I thought about it for a bit I could find a way to do it iteratively with map() instead of hard coding all those mutates. But whatever, moving on!

```{r Load_Samp_Polys}
#| echo: True
#| eval: True

# Read in the sample polys as vectors
samp_vect_list <- list.files("./data/sample_polys/", full.names = T) %>% 
  map(vect)

# Combine them into one vector
samps <- reduce(samp_vect_list, rbind)

# Sanity check
plotRGB(rgb2, stretch = "linear")
polys(samps)
text(samps, samps$type)
```

Now let's sample some points from within these polygons.

```{r Samp_Points}
#| echo: True
#| eval: True

# Make reproducible
set.seed(69)

# Generate the points within the sample polygons
samp_points <- spatSample(samps, 200, method = "random")

# Sanity check
plot(samp_points, "type")
```

Points are generated. Next step is to extract the reflectance values at each point.

```{r Extract_Values}
#| echo: True
#| eval: True

vals <- extract(rgb2, samp_points, method = "bilinear", ID = F)

```

Damnit. I am an idiot. A quarter or more of my `vals` are NA because I forgot to make sure that all my polygons actually fall on the raster. Significant numbers do not, so I need to go back and draw new polygons.

```{r Boundaries}
#| echo: True
#| eval: True

bounds <- boundaries(rgb2)

```
